about:
Mid-State Machine Products operates as a division of Precision Holdings from its headquarters in Winslow, Maine, with additional facilities in Cincinnati, Ohio, and Phoenix, Arizona. Precision Holdings was acquired by private equity firm Insight Equity in 2014; Insight Equity, headquartered in Southlake, Texas, makes control investments in middle-market manufacturing and distribution businesses. The founding date and original founders of Mid-State Machine Products are not publicly disclosed.

The company provides turnkey manufacturing services spanning engineering, machining, fabrication, assembly, finishing, and testing. Precision Holdings’ combined footprint exceeds 250,000 square feet of manufacturing space, with capacity to produce the most complex components and assemblies for aerospace, defense, power generation, and oil and gas applications. Employee count and production volumes are not disclosed.

The customer base spans military aerospace, commercial aerospace, defense, power generation, and oil and gas sectors. Mid-State focuses on mission‑critical parts and complex assemblies for those industries.

Mid-State emphasizes its full‑suite, turnkey approach as a differentiator, allowing customers to consolidate engineering through test under one roof.

name: Mid-West Textile LLC
old_description: At Mid-West Textile LLC, repurpose, reuse, recycle is more than an Earth Day mantra, it’s our everyday operations.
about:
Mid-West Textile LLC operates from El Paso, Texas, where it has established itself as one of the largest textile recyclers in the United States. The company's founding year is not publicly disclosed, but its business was built on a handshake and a promise to provide customers with a diverse selection of value-added products.

The company's vertically integrated model spans grading, retail, and brokerage services. It collects and grades post-consumer textiles for its own product lines and offers fulfillment, packaging, and shipping capabilities to other vendors. Its expansive grading and brokerage operations allow it to process large volumes of used clothing and textiles, though specific facility size and headcount figures are not published.

Mid-West Textile serves a range of industrial and retail customers, including fiber reclamation operators, industrial wiping cloth suppliers, vintage clothing boutiques, and thrift retail stores. By creating new supply chains for these organizations, the company helps divert millions of pounds of textile waste from landfills each year.

The firm emphasizes that its vertical integration reduces costs and streamlines operations, while its core mission is to reduce post-consumer waste and give new purpose to materials that would otherwise be discarded.

about:
Middleton Equipment Sales, LLC operates from Farmington, New Hampshire. The company's founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

The business functions as an equipment dealer, offering a range of forestry, wood-processing, and construction machinery. Its product lineup includes sawmills from Lucas, North Forest, and Thomas; Pitbulls screeners; sHoule land levelers, rock buckets, and snow plows; TAJFUN winches; Split Fire hydraulic wood splitters; Black professional-grade splitters; White Mountain trailers fabricated in Barnstead, New Hampshire; North Forest wood processors; Tajfun ergonomic winches; dedicated slabbers; Jolex and N&N dump trailers; Palax debris cleaners; and KS12-9 and XN2.0 excavators. The company also facilitates financing through partners such as Sheffield Financial and OneMain Financial.

Customers span logging contractors, firewood producers, sawmill operators, landscapers, and agricultural enterprises throughout the Northeast. The equipment is suited for timber harvesting, land clearing, firewood processing, and site preparation.

The company has not published a formal mission statement or specific differentiators beyond the breadth of brands represented and the availability of financing options.

name: Midwest Bus Parts
old_description: Your trusted nationwide source for OEM and aftermarket school bus parts. Thousands of in-stock parts, expert support, fast shipping and decades of proven reliability.
about:
Midwest Bus Parts was founded in 2004 in Big Lake, Minnesota, as a family-owned and operated business. The company began with a focus on supplying OEM and aftermarket school bus parts to transportation professionals across the United States and internationally.

The company operates a warehouse stocked with thousands of school bus components, ranging from DEF tanks and brake assemblies to lighting, seating, and safety equipment. It offers expert part identification through VIN lookup and technical guidance, and processes orders for same-day shipping on in-stock items with daily nationwide dispatch.

Its customer base includes school districts, private contractors, fleet maintenance operations, and transit operators of all sizes, from large fleets to individual bus owners. The company serves both conventional and transit-style buses, providing parts for brands such as Blue Bird, IC Bus, Thomas Built, and Collins.

Midwest Bus Parts emphasizes a “can-do” attitude, problem-solving, and honest service as core values. It differentiates itself through real-time expert support, a broad selection of OEM and aftermarket options, and a commitment to fast, reliable delivery that keeps buses on the road.

name: Midwest Medical Service
old_description: Midwest Medical Service is a family owned Medical supply and equipment company.
about:
Midwest Medical Service operates from Watertown, South Dakota, as a family-owned medical supply and equipment company. The business has served the region for more than three decades, building its reputation on customer service and hands-on work. Paul Johnson serves as a primary contact for the operation.

The company supplies and rents a range of durable medical equipment including wheelchairs, walkers, bathroom safety products, stair lifts, oxygen systems, CPAP devices for sleep apnea, and bedroom and seating aids. Beyond product distribution, Midwest Medical provides onsite service and repair for equipment, handles home modification installations, and coordinates insurance billing for covered items as a Medicare-participating provider.

Customers are primarily home health-care patients and caregivers seeking mobility, respiratory, and accessibility solutions. The firm works with most major insurance plans and Medicare, serving individuals who need equipment for aging in place, post-acute recovery, or chronic condition management across eastern South Dakota and surrounding areas.

The owners attribute the company's longevity to three pillars—People, Product, and Process—and emphasize personalized service, insurance navigation, and local onsite support as key differentiators.

name: Midwest Precision Molding
old_description: Proud to Be Wisconsin's Leading Provider of Plastic Injection Molding
about:
Midwest Precision Molding operates from a 65,000-square-foot facility in Lake Geneva, Wisconsin. The company has provided plastic injection molding services for over 40 years, with CEO Larry Austin the business since at least 2016 when he acquired Tri-Tec Corp. in nearby Darien and expanded the Plasti-Coil building. The firm began as a specialist in coil winding bobbins and grew into a full-service custom molder.

The shop runs more than 40 injection molding presses, including 11 Sodick machines and new automation cells, supported by an on-site tool room. Core capabilities include tight-tolerance molding of gears, bobbins, and insert-overmolded parts, plus a recently added Bausano extrusion line for tubing. Secondary operations such as terminal and pin insertion are performed on specialized equipment, and the company reports producing millions of bobbins annually across high- and low-volume projects.

Customers range from global manufacturers needing precision gears and assemblies to electronics producers requiring custom coil-winding bobbins. The company emphasizes collaboration from product design and material selection through post-production, serving any project size without minimum order constraints mentioned.

MPM positions itself as Wisconsin's only true custom molder focused on tight-tolerance precision parts, a distinction reinforced by its ISO 9001:2015 certified quality system and UL Assurance Seal. The business was built to keep injection molding and moldmaking in the Midwest, offering in-house tooling and rapid response from concept to delivery.

about:
Midwest Solutions Inc is based in Antioch, Illinois, and operates across the Midwest. The company began as a local solar installation operation before evolving into a full-service engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) partner. No founding year or founders are disclosed in public materials.

The firm delivers end-to-end solar project execution, covering engineering, permitting, procurement of tier‑1 equipment, installation, and project management. Its services include residential solar installation, energy storage systems, community solar programs, and EPC support for solar dealers. The company does not publish facility size, headcount, or annual volume figures.

Midwest Solutions serves solar dealers and professionals seeking a scalable EPC partner, as well as homeowners who want a guided path to solar adoption. Concrete examples include residential rooftop installations, battery backup systems, and community solar subscriptions across Illinois and neighboring Midwestern states.

The company emphasizes local permitting expertise, predictable project timelines, transparent communication, and a partner‑first approach as its key differentiators. It states that its Midwest‑focused knowledge of utility requirements and weather‑ready system design reduces delays and improves outcomes.

about:
Midwestern Energy Solutions, doing business as MW Energy DBA, is headquartered in West Burlington, Iowa, at 11208 143rd Avenue. The company provides electrical, HVAC, solar, generator, and roofing services to customers throughout Iowa, Illinois, and Missouri. No founding year or ownership details are disclosed on its website.

The firm’s licensed electricians handle residential and commercial electrical work including wiring, troubleshooting, service upgrades, and emergency repairs. Its HVAC division offers installation, maintenance, and repair of heating and cooling systems. The company also installs and services solar photovoltaic systems, battery storage, and backup generators, and it recently added roofing to its service lineup. A 24/7 emergency service line operates alongside normal business hours of 7:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

Midwestern Energy Solutions serves homeowners, commercial businesses, and industrial facilities in a wide corridor of the Midwest. Its stated service area includes Burlington, Danville, Mediapolis, Galesburg, Ottumwa, Macomb, Keokuk, Fort Madison, Fairfield, Kahoka, Quincy, Iowa City, Cedar Rapids, Peoria, and Davenport.

The company states that its goal is to deliver the highest level of customer satisfaction through quality work and lasting solutions for all electrical needs, and to provide clean, renewable energy that saves customers money and benefits the planet.

Mill Direct Textiles operates from Somersworth, New Hampshire, where it maintains an exclusive relationship with Polartec to supply fabrics without minimum order requirements. The company leverages this partnership to offer three distinct inventory tiers: Regular Stock items purchased as production runs, Limited Stock consisting of Excess First Quality and Merchantable Seconds, and Aged First Quality rolls held for more than two years and sold as-is at deep discounts.

The business functions as a fabric distributor, managing a warehouse on the Salmon Falls River It provides inspection services, sample yardage through its sister company MillYardage.com, pre-order management for regular stock, and in-store pickup for local customers. A resourceful customer service team assists with swatch selection, cost-effective logistics, and locating hard-to-find styles.

Customers range from growing businesses to returning buyers seeking Polartec fabrics for applications such as base layers, insulation, and weather protection. The company highlights styles like PowerGrid, Thermal Pro, and WindPro, serving makers of outdoor apparel, performance gear, and other textile-based products.

Mill Direct Textiles emphasizes its no-minimum policy, exclusive Polartec access, and responsive service as key differentiators. The team works directly with buyers to match fabric styles to project needs, offering both steady supply and bargain opportunities through its varied stock categories.
